submitter: leopardess3 / cta_link_integrity workstream (resubmission — v1 round was voided by bugs_open/019, not by a verdict)
rationale:
BE CONCISE. A short decisive review beats a thorough one here: a reviewer whose output hits the token cap voids the ENTIRE round and discards every other seat's work (bugs_open/019 — that is what killed the previous attempt at this submission, not a verdict). Name your decision and your single strongest objection; do not restate the plan back to me.

ARBITRATE between two remedies. I have a preference with low confidence; the owner asked for a direction rather than my instinct. Answer the four questions at the end briefly — one or two sentences each.

PROBLEM (diagnosis c84940fb, verdict CONFIRMED). A CTA destination written into resolved_data by resolve_internal_links at build time is re-derived by plan_sections on every later render for any field whose source is query-resolved (site_specs.*, pages.*, site_assets.*, config.*), because sourceResolver.resolve re-runs its lookups fresh with nothing cached. The resolver computes the right destination and it is overwritten. Measured live: 83 of 119 derived CTA url fields (18 components) are vulnerable; 13 are immune via the renderer/static guard; 21 are source:llm.

STANDING REMEDY, AND WHY I DISTRUST IT. Migrate url fields to source 'renderer' one component at a time, while keeping the hardcoded ctaFieldNames map in lockstep. Two hand-maintained lists that must agree for a button to be repairable — amended by four migrations (091, 096, 097b, 098) teaching the same lesson. The map covers 5 of the 33 component functions that declare CTA url fields. Everything outside it is, in the code's own words, 'detectable but not repairable'.

OPTION B (this plan). Derive CTA url fields from input_schema — any *_url with a sibling *_label/*_text — in ONE shared helper used at the three call sites that currently disagree. Retires both lists.

OPTION A (the alternative). Keep the architecture; run a fifth migration flipping the 83 fields to 'renderer'. No Go change, live immediately, far less invasive.

QUESTIONS I CANNOT ANSWER MYSELF.
1. Option B changes plan_sections, a hot path on every page build on every site. Is that blast radius justified to retire a migration pattern, or is it trading a known maintenance cost for an unknown correctness risk?
2. Is the sibling-label rule a durable contract, or merely a description of today's naming conventions?
3. Does a migration written four times make a fifth pragmatic, or is the repetition itself the defect?
4. Go changes are inert until an image roll; option A is live immediately. Does that asymmetry decide it? I have not weighted it confidently.

I would rather be told option A is correct than be approved into a change I flagged as risky.

plan.summary: A button destination computed at build time is silently overwritten on the next render, because plan_sections re-derives any query-resolved field and merges last. The workaround has been per-component migration to source 'renderer' plus a hardcoded ctaFieldNames map kept in step — two lists, four migrations, covering 5 of 33 CTA-bearing components. This replaces both with one schema-derived definition shared by the three call sites. Alternative explicitly offered: a fifth migration instead (see rationale, option A).

edits.rationale: One definition of 'this field is a button destination' so the three consumers cannot drift apart again — the same reason links.go was consolidated after three callers each decided 'is this an internal link' differently.
The exclusion case is the one I got wrong in the written spec before testing it: a naive '*_url' rule captures guide_image_url and logo_url. Pin it.

Lets a button-bearing component be repairable without being hand-added to a map. STAGED: this round only LOGS the derived-vs-mapped delta and changes nothing written, because derivation takes this action from ~10 fields to potentially 119. The write switches over after one real build's log is read.

THE CONTESTED EDIT — judge this hardest. Makes plan_sections yield ownership of CTA url fields to the resolver, instead of requiring each component to be migrated to 'renderer' individually. This is what retires the four-times-rewritten migration; it is also a behaviour change in a hot path on every page build on every site.
edits.sketch:
// in the per-field loop, BEFORE the query-resolved branch:
+ // CTA url fields are owned by resolve_internal_links, which resolves them
+ // against the real pages set. Re-deriving here overwrites that and merges
+ // last — how a correct destination gets silently replaced (diagnosis
+ // c84940fb). A declared fallback is still honoured so a component that has
+ // never been through the resolver is not left with a bare button.
+ if ctaOwnedURLFields[fieldName] {
+   if fallback != nil { resolvedData[fieldName] = fallback }
+   continue
+ }

ctaOwnedURLFields is built once per section from
datahelpers.DeriveCTAURLFields(comp.InputSchema).

REVIEWER: the alternative is to leave this file untouched and migrate the 83
vulnerable fields' source to 'renderer' instead. Please say which.

edits.rationale: The repair path consults the same map, so repair scope has always been narrower than detection scope — misdirected_cta scans anchors on every component while only six could ever be repaired. Closes that gap in the same move.
edits.sketch:
- fields, isCTA := ctaFieldNames[function]
- if !isCTA { return false }
+ fields := ctaURLFieldsFor(function, comp) // shared helper; map as override
+ if len(fields) == 0 { return false }

Keep-rule UNCHANGED: an authored URL that is real, non-excluded and
non-circular is kept; only phantom/excluded/circular/empty are replaced.
Widening what is REPAIRABLE must not widen what is OVERWRITTEN.

grounded_in: plan_sections_action.go:1211 — `if source == "renderer" || source == "static" || strings.HasPrefix(source, "renderer.") || strings.HasPrefix(source, "static.") { if fallback != nil { resolvedData[fieldName] = fallback }; continue }`

resolve_internal_links_action.go:83-90 — `a button-bearing component missing from this set is detectable but not repairable` ... `A component added here must ALSO have its url fields' schema source flipped to "renderer" (migrations 091, 098): a site_specs.*/pages.*/static source is re-resolved into resolved_data on every render and merges last`

Diagnosis c84940fb (CONFIRMED) — `The fields that DO get freshly re-queried on every plan_sections call (and so can overwrite a value resolve_internal_links previously wrote into resolved_data) are exactly those whose source string reaches sourceResolver.resolve() — site_specs.*, pages.*, site_assets.*, or config.* — not 'static'.`

Live library 2026-07-19: 119 derived CTA url fields across 33 component functions; ctaFieldNames covers 5 of the 33; by source 83 query-resolved (vulnerable), 13 renderer/static, 21 llm. Without the sibling-label test a naive '*_url' rule additionally captures 32 site_assets.image/logo fields.
plan.risks:
1. The plan_sections edit is in a hot path on every page build on every site; a wrong field set there suppresses legitimate source resolution. Mitigated by the sibling-label test and by honouring declared fallbacks. A reviewer should check the case of a component that legitimately wants its CTA url from site_specs as deliberate site config — I believe that case IS the bug (it is what locked 143 of 144 buttons to /contact.html) but I may be wrong.
2. The derivation rule may describe today's naming conventions rather than a durable contract. A component naming a destination without a matching label silently drops out of both detection and repair — the map's failure mode, moved rather than removed.
3. applyCTARecompute widens the repairable field set; the keep-rule is deliberately unchanged so widening what is repairable does not widen what is overwritten. Check I have not accidentally done both.
